messages:
anya: Heads-up — I'm experimenting with an eviction-based routing shim for noisy SLOs. want a quick sanity check on telemetry exports, notify behavior, and ownership before I draft an RFC.

matt: eviction-based routing = demote to lower fanout / fallback model variant on high noise? or do you mean evict requests to a cheaper tier?

anya: Right now proof-of-concept is: detect sustained noisy signal -> mark tenant as 'evicted' (soft degrade) -> route new requests to fallback variant and reduce notify fanout. basic rule: `if burn_rate > 0.5 && noise_score > 0.7 for 5m then mark_evicted`. Example proto: `{"policy":"evict_if_burn>0.5 && noise>0.7","grace_period_s":300}`

oliver: Telemetry question: will we emit per-tenant eviction events to a topic? need a stable event name and request anchor so we can correlate traces/kv cache and SLO deltas. Suggest `slo.eviction.v1` with fields: tenant_id, reason, sample_trace_id.

frida: Console/UX thought — please don't show the word "evicted" to customers. It's alarming. prefer "degraded routing" with clear guidance and a prominent link to what to do. Also need to show when notifications are suppressed and who owns the suppression.

matt: Also important: what happens to alerts. If we demote and quiet notify for 10m we could hide a real regression. Do we suppress entirely or route to a lower escalation path (e.g., only page platform on persistent degradation)?

anya: Implementation plan I'm leaning to: eviction -> soft-fallback model variant + set `notify: quiet` for N minutes (default 10m) but emit `slo.eviction.v1` event and create a telemetry anchor. Quota accounting stays the same, but an exposure card will show the degraded routing and a counter `evictions_in_1h`.

kevin: worry: suppression hides signal. Can we gate suppression with a quality check? Example: only quiet notifications if quality_change < 0.02 (relative) over the last 30m, and noise_score above threshold. i.e. `suppress = noise > 0.7 && quality_delta < 0.02`. That way we avoid hiding real regressions.

sre-bot: incident-bot: auto-create alert when `evictions_in_1h > 5` for any tenant — will post to #incidents.

frida: From product side we need API fields: `eviction_reason`, `suppress_until`, and a human-readable `ui_hint`. Console should show timeline + link to telemetry. Also require an opt-out toggle per-tenant: some customers must not be auto-degraded.

anya: Agreed. API change proposal: PATCH `/api/v1/tenants/:id/slo-routing` adding optional fields: `eviction_reason`, `suppress_until`, `schema_version`. Keep fields optional for backward compat.

oliver: compatibility note: make new fields optional and non-breaking. include `schema_version` on events as well so ingestion can evolve. Also add `sample_trace_id` so SRE can jump to a trace.

matt: I'll draft an RFC with rollout plan: start with 2% tenants for 2 weeks, telemetry-only (no suppression) -> 10% with suppression gated by quality_delta rule -> full rollout. Also include a rollback knob in the console.

frida: I'll wire up a mock of the console card (degraded routing + manual override + timeline + telemetry anchors). Want to pair on the telemetry schema tomorrow 10am?

anya: yes please — 10am works for me. I'll also add ownership field to the eviction event so we know who created the suppression (system vs operator).

matt: :thumbsup: Thanks team — RFC draft incoming.

frida: small nit: make sure the console link deep-links into our logs explorer with `eviction_reason` filter so support can jump straight to relevant logs.

anya: will add that to the RFC.
